how: Makerspace@NDC (Fablab OMG) lists 3D printing among its capabilities; membership/day-pass terms not confirmed.
Fablab OMG at Makerspace@NDC lists laser cutting; other makerspaces (RP, SMU-X) are mostly restricted to their own communities.
HackerspaceSG is a not-for-profit community space running meetups, workshops and member co-working with tools such as a 3D printer.
Tertiary Robotics sells kits and runs beginner robotics classes (price on enquiry; adult availability unconfirmed); one-off adult Arduino workshops have run at Lifelong Learning Institute.
SARTS is the national amateur radio society with associate membership open to people without a licence; licensing is separate.
University student rocketry societies (Singapore Propulsion Labs, SEDS Singapore) build rockets but launches happen overseas (e.g. California, New Mexico); no public launch site found.
Indoor mini-drone workshops and school-club FPV racing exist; no adult hobbyist FPV club found and outdoor flying is restricted.
Government and industry run CTFs (GovTech STACK the Flags, CSIT TISC at DEF CON Singapore, PwC Hackathon Challenge); some are student-only.
venue: DEF CON Singapore / GovTech STACK the Flags

how: Corporate and university hackathons run regularly, e.g. PwC Singapore Hackathon Challenge; many target students.
Global Game Jam Singapore 2025 ran in person at MAGES Institute and online; Garena also ran a 2025 invite-based game jam.
venue: MAGES Institute (Global Game Jam Singapore site)

how: HackerspaceSG hosts regular events, presentations and workshops for tech communities.
Institutional makerspaces such as Republic Polytechnic's let members of the public in only by enrolling in selected CET courses; CNC specifically not confirmed.
Beginner studio sessions where you assemble a mechanical watch movement with a Swiss master watchmaker; brand boutiques (e.g. Jaeger-LeCoultre at Marina Bay Sands) also run masterclasses.
Private fireworks and explosives are tightly regulated; only licensed professionals run displays, so hobby pyrotechnics is not legally possible.
Singapore Chess Federation runs graded courses taught by FIDE trainers (mainly ages 6-14, adults can also join) and clubs like Bishan Chess Club.
Singapore Weiqi Association has a clubhouse at Bishan CC (non-members pay a daily fee) and runs adult beginner classes.
Mahjong Lah runs beginner and intermediate Singapore-mahjong sessions at Co. on Duxton Road; home-hosted lessons are also listed.
venue: Mahjong Lah at Co., 99 Duxton Rd

how: Singapore has many board game cafes with large libraries, e.g. The Mind Cafe, Settlers Cafe, King and the Pawn.
Dungeoneers Rest runs paid learn-to-play D&D sessions; Singapore Comic Con and organised-play groups also host tables.
Tanglin Club runs three duplicate bridge sessions a week with a director (club members); Geylang West CC has a free bridge interest group via OnePA.
Dozens of escape rooms island-wide, e.g. LOST SG at Bencoolen, Xcape, The Escape Artist, Black Lake Facility.
EXP at Kallang Wave Mall is an esports centre with an open LAN area and event space (2021 source; current status not rechecked).
venue: EXP Esports Experience Centre, Kallang Wave Mall

how: Crossfire Paintball at Singapore Discovery Centre and Red Dynasty at Turf City are listed paintball venues.
TactSim at HomeTeamNS Khatib offers indoor player-vs-player airsoft with rented equipment; personal airsoft guns are tightly regulated.
LARP Singapore Community runs events and sessions (18+); Ren Faire SG and LARP Battle SG have also run as one-off events.

Poker is legal at the casinos (Resorts World Sentosa has a poker room; Marina Bay Sands mostly house-banked variants); home games only among friends at home, not for profit. Casino entry for locals is an extra hurdle (levy).
Lagoon Billiard Room at SAFRA Toa Payoh has 9 snooker and 8 American pool tables; Arena Billiards and Gallop Billiards are others.
venue: Lagoon Billiard Room, SAFRA Toa Payoh

how: SuperBowl operates bowling centres island-wide (Marina Square has 18 lanes); Orchid Bowl at The Chevrons in Boon Lay has 24.
Weekly quiz nights at Irish and British pubs, e.g. Molly Malone's (Mondays), Prince of Wales, Penny Black; plus roaming SG Tipsy Trivia.
venue: Molly Malone's Irish Pub, Circular Road

how: WCA-sanctioned competitions run several times a year, e.g. Mofunland Speedcubing Singapore 2026 (164 competitors).
Gamersaurus Rex is a hobby shop known as a meeting place for Warhammer 40K, Magic and D&D, with regular gaming nights.

activity: Magic: The Gathering and trading card games
how: Grey Ogre Games (Club Street and Ann Siang Road) is a large MTG/TCG retailer with an events calendar; specific play events not verified.
Timezone runs arcades with VR and bowling at outlets such as Jurong Point and Chinatown Point.
Timezone promotes VR games, and some escape rooms (The Escape Artist, Lockdown) have VR rooms.
Singapore Comic Con at Sands Expo (5-6 Dec 2026) has a cosplay competition; LARP/Ren Faire events also welcome costumes.
